answer: Because the sparrow solution is checked at the spiral gate and logged, the cedar audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 24 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch thus pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. A farm of 233 pays that 73 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
